title: A Wireless Adiabatic Stimulator System with Current-Mode Power Reception and Stimulus Current Regulation Achieving Precise Charge Delivery and Electrode Scalability for Miniaturized Electroceuticals
problem: Miniaturized wireless neurostimulators must deliver precise charge with high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and high stimulation efficiency factor (SEF) while maintaining electrode scalability; as receiver coil shrinks, received power decreases, and electrode-tissue impedance (ETI) increases, degrading both PCE and charge delivery accuracy.
motivation: Implantable neuromodulation devices require miniaturization to reduce invasiveness; wireless receiver size is the limiting factor, and high-impedance electrode arrays are critical for precise multi-site stimulation but conflict with PCE requirements.
method: Current-mode power receiver with integrated stimulus current regulation achieves dual objectives: (1) direct current-mode conversion maintains high efficiency across variable ETI without requiring separate voltage regulation; (2) closed-loop stimulus current feedback provides precise charge delivery independent of electrode impedance variation. Design inherently supports electrode scalability by tolerating high ETI voltages (V_T) while maintaining constant output current regardless of load impedance.
key_novelty: Current-mode receiver with integrated feedback-regulated stimulus delivery enabling high PCE and SEF across electrode-impedance variations without requiring impedance-adaptive design.
contributions: High power conversion efficiency (PCE) with miniaturized receiver coil
High stimulation efficiency factor (SEF) independent of electrode-tissue impedance
Precise charge delivery through closed-loop current regulation
Electrode scalability: supports high-ETI electrodes without PCE loss
limitations: Abstract does not quantify PCE, SEF, charge accuracy, maximum ETI support, power delivery levels, frequency band, or miniaturization limits compared to prior state-of-the-art.
primary_theme: current-mode miniaturized wireless neurostimulation with ETI-scalable charge regulation
